title: Three Trays, One Oven
story: For the street festival, three families agreed to bake in one kitchen, because the hall oven was already booked. Aunt Rosa brought savoury pastries from her coastal hometown, and the Nguyen family brought a rice cake that needed a low, gentle heat. The pastries wanted a short burst of a hotter oven. Mina wrote the order on a strip of paper and taped it to the cupboard. The cake would go first, then the pastries, then jam buns a neighbour had dropped off. They set a phone alarm for each change so nobody would trust memory alone. When the hall opened, every dish was labelled with its name and its main ingredients. A child asked why the rice cake was only faintly sweet. Mina said it was meant to follow the salty pastries, not to compete with the buns. People took a little of each, which was the sharing the families had wanted.

vocabulary.definition: A public celebration with shared events.
Tasting salty or spiced rather than sweet.
The foods that are used to make a dish.
To try to stand out more than something else.
Marked with a name or a short description.

quiz.question: In what order were the foods baked?
options: The cake first, then the pastries, then the jam buns
The jam buns first and the cake not at all
Only the pastries, for the whole afternoon
The cake and the pastries at the same moment
quiz.correctAnswer: The cake first, then the pastries, then the jam buns
quiz.explanation: The cake would go first, then the pastries, then the jam buns.
quiz.supportingSentence: The cake would go first, then the pastries, then jam buns a neighbour had dropped off.

quiz.question: Why did they set an alarm for each change of food?
options: They did not want to rely on memory alone
The hall oven had to be booked again
A child had asked them to hide the cake
The pastries needed to stay hot all day
quiz.correctAnswer: They did not want to rely on memory alone
quiz.explanation: They set a phone alarm for each change so nobody would trust memory alone.
quiz.supportingSentence: They set a phone alarm for each change so nobody would trust memory alone.

quiz.question: Why was the rice cake only slightly sweet?
options: It was meant to follow salty food, not to outdo the buns
The families had no sweet ingredients left
Mina had left it in a cold oven
A child had asked for it to taste like jam
quiz.correctAnswer: It was meant to follow salty food, not to outdo the buns
quiz.explanation: Mina said the cake was meant to follow the salty pastries and not compete with the buns.
quiz.supportingSentence: Mina said it was meant to follow the salty pastries, not to compete with the buns.

quiz.question: How can you tell the families got the sharing they wanted?
options: People took a little food from each dish
One child ate only the jam buns
The hall oven booking was cancelled
The name cards were taken off the table
quiz.correctAnswer: People took a little food from each dish
quiz.explanation: People took a little of each, which was the sharing the families had wanted.
quiz.supportingSentence: People took a little of each, which was the sharing the families had wanted.

quiz.question: What does savoury mean in this story?
options: Salty or spiced rather than sweet
Baked for a very long time
Written on a paper label
Shared among three families
quiz.correctAnswer: Salty or spiced rather than sweet
quiz.explanation: The savoury pastries are the salty ones the cake was meant to follow, so they are not a sweet food.
quiz.supportingSentence: Aunt Rosa brought savoury pastries from her coastal hometown, and the Nguyen family brought a rice cake that needed a low, gentle heat.
